newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian LNG opens talks with Portuguese gas firm.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian LNG opens talks with Portuguese gas firm.

text.p: Nigerian liquefied natural gas (NLNG) company said on Tuesday it had opened preliminary discussions with Portuguese state-owned Transgas company which plans to buy its natural gas.

"We are considering the sale of 0.5 billion cubic metres per year to be delivered to Transgas via the Huelva receiving facilities of Enagas in Spain," Steve Ollerearnshaw, NLNG's British managing director, told a news conference in Lagos.
NLNG a fortnight ago denied a Portuguese newspaper report that it had started talks with Transgas.
"As at that time it was merely speculative, it's only recently that we began discussions," Ollerearnshaw said, adding that delivery would start on start-up of the NLNG plant in 1999.

Nigeria's $4 billion LNG project, now in full swing in the southeastern oil-producing area of Bonny, is expected to produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of LNG per year from a plant projected to start production in 1999.
Ollerearnshaw said the volume of gas that could be sold to Transgas was separate from the yearly 3.5 billion cubic metres volume which Italian state-owned utility firm Enel had contracted to buy.

Enel in December cancelled the long-term contract to buy the Nigerian LNG, citing its abandonment of a project to construct a gas plant at Montalto di Castro, north of Rome, for economic, technical and environmental reasons.
Arbitration proceedings were immediately launched in Switzerland by NLNG following the cancellation.
Oil minister Dan Etete said last week after visiting Italy that Enel had reversed its decision and was now ready to take the entire volume of gas it signed for.
"All issues have been resolved and the Italian government is fully in support of the Nigerian LNG project," Etete said.

But Ollerearnshaw said: "We want to reiterate that NLNG is still awaiting specific written proposals from Enel regarding the ways in which they will receive and pay for the LNG it originally signed to buy from Nigeria."

"Not until we have ironed out all the issues, we cannot say the problem had been resolved. And for the avoidance of doubt, arbitration proceedings between both parties on the cancelled contract are still on."
Partners in the LNG project are the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation, Shell Gas BV, Elf Aquitaine and Italy's Agip SpA
Long-term supply contracts have been signed with Enagas of Spain, Gaz de France and Botas of Turkey.
